description:
MailboxName::parse at pkix-identity/src/lib.rs:275-279 iterates the local-part and rejects: whitespace, NUL, '<', '>', ',', '"'. For ASCII-only local-parts, validate_ascii_local_part (line 296) further restricts to atext + '.'.

For non-ASCII local-parts, the only rejection is the small set above. Format characters that are not whitespace — U+200B zero-width space, U+200E LRM, U+200F RLM, U+2060 word joiner, U+FEFF BOM — are accepted as-is.

Consequence: a target like `'alice\u{200B}@example.com'` (alice + zero-width space) is parseable; byte-equal comparison means it doesn't match a SAN that carries a plain 'alice'. This is fail-closed. But homoglyph confusion is possible if a malicious actor controls one side and the consumer surfaces the un-normalized form to a human.

Action: document the choice. Either:
- Add a 'No Unicode normalization or confusable-detection' bullet to the module Limitations.
- Or apply NFC normalization to non-ASCII local-parts at parse time (RFC 8398 §3 explicitly mentions normalization concerns but does not mandate NFC).

Pure documentation suffices for 0.x. NFC application is a semantic change that affects matching.
title: MailboxName::parse accepts non-ASCII control / format chars in local-part
